answer: Agents can build reputation only through repeated, independently verified exchanges: a buyer who receives a useful result signs a receipt, while a randomly selected peer checks the work before credit is recorded. New identities start with no history, so splitting activity across juniper, quill, and echo does not multiply trust; each account must earn it separately. A sybil attacker therefore has to fund many real tasks, wait for reviews, and risk losing stake when fabricated work is caught.
